1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a ring oscillator configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;
one or more logic circuits operatively coupled to the ring oscillator and including:
a first circuit element that receives the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator;
a second circuit element that applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function or hash function to generate a second entropy value;
a third circuit element that seeds a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
a fourth circuit element that generates a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
a fifth circuit element that produces a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number;
wherein the system is configured to implement countermeasures against phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the fifth circuit element being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number, and wherein the countermeasures include applying the plurality of independent first entropy values through the permutation function or hash function prior to seeding the pseudorandom number generator.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the fifth circuit element being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators, and the first circuit element is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent ring oscillators.

5. (Cancelled)

6. (Cancelled)

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the second circuit element applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function.

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the second circuit element is configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the second circuit element applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a hash function.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the second circuit element applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a bit-mixer.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the second circuit element is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function or hash function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the second circuit element is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the permutation function or hash function to generate the second entropy value.

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a ring oscillator;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function or hash function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value;
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number; and
implementing countermeasures against phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator through the application of the permutation function or hash function.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent ring oscillators.

17. (Cancelled)

18. (Cancelled)

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

24. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
